title: Digital design system / component specimens

location.series: Jessie W. Lee / Verizon Master Brand Redesign

slide_intent: Compare type, controls, icons and feedback together so a digital interface can carry one visual language while keeping functions distinct.
strategic_value: A common component vocabulary can connect Verizon’s brand expression to routine digital interactions.
demonstration: A white board groups typography sizes, button spacing, navigation rows, scalable eye icons, a chart key and colored notification banners.
practical_value: Compare component anatomy and semantic feedback colors separately from the primary brand palette.

content_islands.name: Interface and data examples
content_islands.spec: Place a basic page, chart legend and black navigation rows at left.

content_islands.name: Type and controls
content_islands.spec: Arrange type-size specimens above paired buttons and three eye-icon scales in the middle.

content_islands.name: Feedback colors
content_islands.spec: Stack blue, green, yellow and orange notification specimens at right with their stated information, confirmation, warning and error roles.

reference_purposes.Application: The board demonstrates typography, navigation, controls, icon scaling and notification roles in interface specimens.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The notification specimens explicitly assign blue to information, green to confirmation, yellow to warning and orange to error.

ingredient.name: Notification color
ingredient.role: Help a user distinguish the kind of feedback.
ingredient.application: Use the specimen’s blue information, green confirmation, yellow warning and orange error assignments.
ingredient.scope: The historical digital component board shown here; these semantic assignments do not redefine the entire brand palette.
